trap.label: hardly = difícil?
trap.wrong: Hardly we had arrived when it rained.
trap.right: Hardly had we arrived when it rained.
trap.why: “Hardly” lembra “dificilmente/duro”, e o brasileiro esquece a inversão e usa before/than. Em inglês: Hardly + had + sujeito + pp … when.

mcq.q: Hardly had the doors opened ___ a crowd rushed in.
Scarcely had we left ___ it rained.
No sooner had it begun ___ it stopped.

fix.wrong: Hardly we had left when it rained.
fix.right: Hardly had we left when it rained.

fix.wrong: Hardly had we left than it rained.
fix.right: Hardly had we left when it rained.

fix.wrong: No sooner had we left when it rained.
fix.right: No sooner had we left than it rained.

rewrite.prompt: Comece com Hardly: “We had just left when it rained.”
rewrite.answer: Hardly had we left when it rained.

rewrite.prompt: Comece com No sooner: “We had just left and it rained.”
rewrite.answer: No sooner had we left than it rained.

rewrite.prompt: Comece com Scarcely: “He had just sat down when she called.”
rewrite.answer: Scarcely had he sat down when she called.
